newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former Labor senator Colston may return - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former Labor senator Colston may return - paper.

text.p: Key Australian Independent senator Mal Colston is considering a move to re-join the Australian Labor Party, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said Labor branches in Colston's Gold Coast base had passed a motion inviting Colston to reapply for membership as long as he was prepared to respect party solidarity.
"Senator Colston responded to the gesture by telling his local newspaper that while he was happy as an Independent, he would consider returning," the newspaper said.

Colston and fellow Independent Brian Harradine are vital to the fate of several important bills as the Liberal-National government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the upper house of parliament, the Senate.
Plans to sell one-third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp is one of these as all other non-government parties in the Senate oppose the sale.
Colston resigned from the Labor Party in August after party powerbrokers declined to support his bid to become Senate deputy president.
"Federal (Labor) sources said Senator Colston would have to resign as Senate deputy president before the parliamentary party would accept his return," the newspaper said.
